---
title: "NFL matchup tool"
pagetitle: "NFL matchup tool: expected margin and win chance"
description: "Pick any two NFL teams and home, away or a neutral site to see the margin and win chance the current team ratings expect, with the range around it."
page-layout: full
---

Pick two teams and where they play. The page works out what the current team ratings expect: a margin with its 80% range and each team's chance to win, through week {{< meta nfl.mu_week >}} of {{< meta nfl.season >}}. It is a reading of the ratings, not a prediction of one game: a typical game misses the expected margin by about {{< meta nfl.mu_mae >}} points. The rating forecasts a margin only, so there is no expected score.

```{=html}
<div class="explorer">
  <div class="controls" id="c"></div>
  <div id="result" class="matchup"><div class="loading">Loading…</div></div>
  <div id="bars" class="plot-host"></div>
  <p class="caption" id="cap"></p>
  <div id="t"></div>
  <p class="caption" id="tcap"></p>
</div>
<script>
(async () => {
  const S = Sparvi, f = S.fmt, U = S.urlState;
  const D = await S.load("/data/nfl/matchup.json");
  const L = D.line, Z80 = 1.2815515655446004;
  const teams = D.teams, byId = new Map(teams.map(t => [t.id, t]));
  const ranked = teams.slice().sort((a, b) => a.rank - b.rank);
  const DEF = { a: ranked[0].id, b: ranked[1].id, site: "n" };
  const st = { a: byId.has(U.get("a")) ? U.get("a") : DEF.a, b: byId.has(U.get("b")) ? U.get("b") : DEF.b,
               site: ["a", "b", "n"].includes(U.get("site")) ? U.get("site") : DEF.site };
  const sgn = (v, d = 1) => (v > 0 ? "+" : v < 0 ? "−" : "") + f.num(Math.abs(v), d);
  // The normal distribution's cumulative probability (Abramowitz and Stegun 7.1.26; error below 2e-7).
  const erf = x => { const s = Math.sign(x), a = Math.abs(x), t = 1 / (1 + 0.3275911 * a);
    return s * (1 - (((((1.061405429 * t - 1.453152027) * t) + 1.421413741) * t - 0.284496736) * t + 0.254829592) * t * Math.exp(-a * a)); };
  // The same arithmetic as nfl/team_efficiency/matchup.py `expected` (a test holds the two equal).
  function expected(a, b, site) {
    const hc = site === "a" ? 1 : site === "b" ? -1 : 0;
    const margin = L.home_points * hc + L.points_per_net * (a.net - b.net);
    return { margin, lo: margin - Z80 * L.margin_sd, hi: margin + Z80 * L.margin_sd, p: 0.5 * (1 + erf(margin / (L.margin_sd * Math.SQRT2))) };
  }
  const opts = teams.map(t => [t.id, t.name]);
  function controls() {
    const A = byId.get(st.a), B = byId.get(st.b);
    document.getElementById("c").replaceChildren(
      S.select("Team A", opts, st.a, v => { st.a = v; controls(); draw(); }),
      S.select("Team B", opts, st.b, v => { st.b = v; controls(); draw(); }),
      S.el("label", {}, "Where", S.seg([["a", `At ${A.name}`], ["n", "Neutral site"], ["b", `At ${B.name}`]], st.site, v => { st.site = v; draw(); })));
  }
  let table = null;
  function draw() {
    const A = byId.get(st.a), B = byId.get(st.b), same = A.id === B.id;
    const x = expected(A, B, st.site);
    const where = st.site === "n" ? "at a neutral site" : `at ${st.site === "a" ? A.name : B.name}`;
    const fav = x.margin >= 0 ? A : B, m = Math.abs(x.margin);
    const res = document.getElementById("result");
    if (same) {
      res.replaceChildren(S.el("p", { class: "page-summary" }, "Pick two different teams."));
      document.getElementById("bars").replaceChildren(); document.getElementById("cap").textContent = "";
    } else {
      res.replaceChildren(
        S.el("p", { class: "matchup-score", id: "score" }, `${fav.name} by ${f.num(m, 1)}`),
        S.el("p", { class: "page-summary", id: "line" },
          `${where[0].toUpperCase() + where.slice(1)}, ${A.name} wins ${f.num(100 * x.p, 0)}% of the time and ${B.name} ${f.num(100 * (1 - x.p), 0)}%.`));
      const rows = [{ team: A.name, p: x.p }, { team: B.name, p: 1 - x.p }];
      S.plot(document.getElementById("bars"), w => Plot.plot({ ...S.plotDefaults(w), height: 120, marginLeft: 180, marginBottom: 40,
        x: { label: "Chance to win →", domain: [0, 1], tickFormat: v => f.num(100 * v, 0) + "%", grid: true },
        y: { label: null, domain: rows.map(r => r.team) },
        marks: [Plot.barX(rows, { y: "team", x: "p", fill: "#0f5257" }), Plot.ruleX([0.5], { stroke: "#16181d", strokeDasharray: "3,3" }),
                Plot.text(rows, { y: "team", x: "p", text: r => f.num(100 * r.p, 0) + "%", dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fontWeight: 600 }),
                Plot.tip(rows, Plot.pointerY({ y: "team", x: "p", title: r => `${r.team}: ${f.num(100 * r.p, 1)}% to win ${where}` }))] }));
      document.getElementById("cap").textContent = `From the ratings through week ${D.through_week} of ${D.season}. The expected margin is ${A.name} ${sgn(x.margin)}; four games in five like this one should land between ${A.name} ${sgn(x.lo)} and ${A.name} ${sgn(x.hi)}. `
        + `The dashed line is an even game. Home field is worth ${f.num(L.home_points, 1)} points; switch the site to see it move.`;
    }
    const cols = [
      { key: "name", label: "Team", align: "l", html: r => S.nflTeamLink(r.id, r.name), sortVal: r => r.name },
      { key: "net", label: "Net rating", fmt: v => sgn(v, 3), title: "Offense less defense, in EPA per play, as the forecast uses it (shrunk toward average)" },
      { key: "off", label: "Offense", fmt: v => sgn(v, 3), title: "EPA per play above average; higher is better" },
      { key: "def", label: "Defense", fmt: v => sgn(v, 3), title: "EPA per play allowed above average; lower is better" },
      { key: "rank", label: "Rank", fmt: v => `${v} of ${teams.length}`, title: "By net rating" },
    ];
    table ||= S.table(document.getElementById("t"), cols, { sortKey: "rank", desc: false, pageSize: 5 });
    table.update(same ? [A] : [A, B]);
    document.getElementById("tcap").textContent = `The two teams' ratings in EPA per play. The expected margin is home field plus ${f.num(L.points_per_net / 100, 1)} points for each 0.01 of net rating between them.`;
    U.set({ a: st.a, b: st.b, site: st.site }, DEF);
  }
  controls(); draw();
})();
</script>
```

::: {.note}
Model version: [{{< meta models.nfl_team_efficiency >}}](https://github.com/matt-hardman15/sparvi-site/tree/main/models/nfl/team_efficiency/card.yml) ({{< meta models.nfl_team_efficiency_status >}}).
:::

<details class="method" id="method">
<summary>Method and caveats</summary>

**The ratings.** Each team's offense and defense in [EPA per play](/learn/epa/), estimated together from this season's plays so that each is measured against the opponents it faced, and shrunk toward average (the fewer games, the more). The net rating is offense less defense. These are the ratings the model's forecast uses; the [team efficiency tool](/nfl/tools/team-efficiency.html) shows schedule-corrected numbers that are not shrunk this way, for describing how teams have played.

**The margin.** Across {{< meta nfl.mu_games >}} games of {{< meta nfl.mu_seasons >}}, each predicted from ratings through the week before, the home team's margin was fitted as home field plus a slope on the gap in net ratings. Home field came out at {{< meta nfl.mu_home_points >}} points and each 0.01 of net rating at {{< meta nfl.mu_points_per_hundredth >}} points. Today the best-rated team, the {{< meta nfl.mu_best >}}, would be favored over the lowest-rated, the {{< meta nfl.mu_worst >}}, by {{< meta nfl.mu_best_vs_worst >}} points at a neutral site.

**The range and the win chance.** Actual margins spread around that expectation with a standard deviation of {{< meta nfl.mu_sd >}} points. The 80% range and the win chance come from a normal distribution with that spread.

**How it has tested.** Predicting each season from a fit on the others, the forecast missed the margin by {{< meta nfl.mu_mae >}} points on average, against {{< meta nfl.mu_mae_home >}} for home field alone. That is a modest edge: most of an NFL result is not in the ratings. This model has not yet been through the site's registered backtest, which is why it carries the label above.

**What it can't tell you.** Who is playing quarterback, injuries, rest, weather, or matchups. The ratings count every game this season the same and know nothing before it. There is no expected score, because the rating forecasts the margin and not points. It is not betting advice and uses no betting lines.

Data: [nflverse](https://github.com/nflverse) play-by-play (CC-BY 4.0). Every team has [its own page](/nfl/teams/).

</details>
